mock_response.body:
For now, there are two things I really don't like about Firefox Multi-Account Containers.

1. When I switch containers, it always opens a new tab instead of focusing on the first existing one or doing something similar. Except, of course, if that container doesn't have any open tabs yet.

2. There is no option in the settings to display only the tabs of the selected container—meaning to hide the tabs of the others.

It is precisely because of these issues that I still use the Conex extension. My only problem with it is that it automatically sorts the containers in alphabetical order, even though that's exactly what I don't want. The old Tab Groups extension was able to do this, but unfortunately, the author didn't update it, so it became unusable.

Because of these exact reasons, I am giving it only 1 star!

parameters.description: How to order the results. By default, the best match for the search words, or with no words, Mozilla's recommended add-ons first and then by users.
parameters.name: sort

options.label: Best match for the search words

parameters.description: The language names, summaries and descriptions come back in. English (US) by default. A listing nobody has translated comes back in its own language.
parameters.name: lang

parameters.description: How many to return on this page, from 1 to 50. 25 by default.
parameters.name: limit

author_names.description: The developers' names, joined with commas.

name.description: The name the developer shows, e.g. 'Raymond Hill'.

username.description: The developer's username. Pass it to 'Get developer profile' or to the Developer filter of 'Search add-ons'.

categories.description: The categories it is filed under.

created.description: When it was first listed (ISO 8601, UTC).

guid.description: The add-on's GUID, the id Firefox itself knows it by, e.g. 'uBlock0@raymondhill.net'.

is_experimental.description: True when its developer has marked it experimental.

last_updated.description: When its developer last updated it (ISO 8601, UTC).

name.description: The add-on's name, in the language asked for.

promoted.description: Mozilla's promotions it is part of.

items.description: recommended, line (made by Mozilla) or spotlight.

rating.description: Its average star rating, from 1 to 5. Empty when nobody has rated it.

rating_count.description: How many people have rated it.

recommended.description: True when it is in Mozilla's Recommended Extensions programme, which Mozilla reviews for security and quality.

requires_payment.description: True when it needs a paid service, other software or extra hardware.

review_count.description: How many of those ratings came with text.

slug.description: The add-on's short name in its address, e.g. 'ublock-origin'. Every other action takes it as the add-on.

summary.description: The one-line summary from its listing, as plain text.

tags.description: The tags its developer gave it.

type.description: extension, statictheme (a theme), dictionary or language (a language pack).

type_label.description: The type in words: Extension, Theme, Dictionary or Language pack.

users.description: How many people use it on an average day, updated daily.

weekly_downloads.description: How many times it was downloaded last week.

works_on_android.description: True when the current version also works in Firefox for Android.

count.description: How many there are in all, across every page.

has_more.description: True when there is another page after this one.

page.description: Which page this is, counting from 1.

page_count.description: How many pages there are at this page size.

suggest_add_ons.description: The add-ons addons.mozilla.org suggests as a name is typed into its search box: up to 10, best match first, each with its slug, type and whether Mozilla recommends it. Quicker than a full search for turning a name into the slug other actions take.
